title: Windows decompilations and eight-bit remakes discovery
summary: Add 22 qualified projects from a 32-repository review; retain scope and fidelity caveats.
notes: Root personally searched C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows. Inspected 30 pinned repository trees and primary documents/source, with two additional repositories deferred because a complete tree was unavailable. Qualified entries and explicit deferrals are distinguished. No discovery worker used. Separate original-author remakes, source preservation, subsystem research and unfinished engines; do not infer fidelity from screenshots or a README claim. No upstream software executed. Pinned bytes are ephemeral local review material only; retained submission carries immutable proof identities without source excerpts.

sources.reason: Compatibility shim rather than a reconstructed game engine. Inspected C replaces WinG calls with GDI and redirects INI/file paths through import hooks; Python tools decode module image and object/path formats. Original TONKA.EXE still executes.

Substantial retail-executable reconstruction with recovered types, game/UI systems and SurRender interfaces. Inspected spell-info dialog uses named spellbook, usage, target and range tables with original-address annotations. Reuses released SGP material under its non-commercial licence.

Substantive Windows fork of richardpenman/civ2. Adds original-media ingestion, native launcher, menus, video/music handling and path adaptations. Inspected fixups reconstruct window procedures and resource cleanup from machine code; this is not a simple unchanged mirror.

Matching-oriented recovery of LEGOLAND (2000), with readable map accessors and original function annotations. README distinguishes exported-function counts from game-code byte coverage and acknowledges WIP functions. Portable-only fixes are guarded separately.

Reconstructs simulator, shell and network binaries, with a separate Matrox edition target. Inspected TargetAttacker uses named AI flags, targets and teammate selection with addresses for both simulator variants. README explicitly says many placeholder names and non-identical functions remain.

Windows matching reconstruction informed by Macintosh debug symbols and cross-version structural comparison. Inspected CGameStatus reconstructs password level-data packing and state handling with meaningful constants. Exact, fuzzy and effective metrics are explicitly separate.

Source-derived native port of CMR2Decomp, replacing platform graphics/audio/input/network/video APIs rather than emulating the CPU. Inspected fixed-point matrix helpers preserve explicit x87 conversion/rounding operations. Widescreen and bug fixes deliberately extend original behaviour.

Native RBR 1.02/NGP reconstruction with typed spring-damper state, explicit x87 precision and recording-based comparison tooling. Inspected physics source separates typed values from binary-layout adapters. The hybrid oracle is a test facility, not evidence that the standalone engine executes guest game code.

Reconstructs lost Turbo Pascal game source from the 1998 executable using Ghidra, prototype/library sources and DOSBox-X comparisons. Inspected weapons code cites original addresses and implements shot allocation, pod reloads and targeting. Classic/remastered renderers share a fixed-tick simulation.

Watcom DOS/4GW executable and data research plus new SDL2 engine for the 1996 arithmetic racer. Named evidence confidence levels distinguish findings from hypotheses. Inspected headless race simulator loads original archives and traces opponent waypoint/finish behaviour.

Small-game recreation collection including Pong, Letter Catcher, Tunnel Journey, Tetris variants and Magic Bunny Hop. Inspected Bunny Hop has explicit power/jump/landing state and success detection; these are semantic remakes, not a C64 CPU wrapper.

Qt game-development study based on C64 Snoopy, with replacement penguin artwork. Inspected movement handler implements jumping, solid-platform collision, death/reset and level exit; author explicitly calls it unfinished.

Seven level modules recreate the C64 challenge structure. Inspected piranha level implements swimming/diving, pursuit, patrol and random fish behaviour with collision tests. No disassembly or original-code derivation established.

Substantive OpenGGS fork with Cardputer-oriented viewport/input/package work and recreated C64-style intro/audio. Inspected stage-zero code builds named tile and letter patterns into the intro stage rather than running C64 instructions.

Explicit first-level recreation with room transitions, inventory pickups, doors, player lives and intro control. Inspected game controller switches active room and input source and handles restart state.

Contest remake with player-selectable JetLee, Ninja and Yamo. Inspected hero code defines movement, attacks, sprite hitboxes and different enemy/player objects. New selectable-character behaviour distinguishes it from binary recovery.

Unity recreation with rocket, fuel, alien and player systems. Inspected GameManager reconstructs death/explosion/respawn and obtains game state from the level loader; no original Z80-code recovery established.

Boriel BASIC settlement, procedural journey and ship-interior adaptation. Source includes a 64-column renderer and explicit game state. Design notes document changed combat/economy, reduced population/map, missing resource tiers, story, sound and save/load.
Native Spectrum reimplementation of Ed Averett’s Videopac/Odyssey 2 game, using z88dk SP1 sprites, asteroid/bullet/UFO state and beeper effects.
Native Spectrum reimplementation with explicit maze geometry, moving pills, ghosts and sprite collision state. Version 0.7 source uses z88dk/SP1 and beeper effects.

Original author expands the 1989 PAW adventure into a browser implementation with more text, locations and an alternate novel-based ending. Inspected JS engine implements PAW-style flags, vocabulary, objects and condacts, with separate authored adventure text.

Native Go/Ebitengine reconstruction with separate ST, HD and Apple II-style presentation. Inspected enemy-course state uses semantic values and explicitly refuses an unproven mode-0/cloak helper, preserving a documented approximation boundary.
Sonic Dream Team is modern macOS/mobile source reconstruction, outside this retro platform pass; explicitly not yet playable.
Pinned tree contains only README, no inspectable remake source; defer source-unavailable archive.
Explicitly runs unmodified game in Z80/Spectrum emulator and draws new graphics from guest memory: game-specific baked emulation, audit-only rather than catalogue addition.
Has separate PS1 matching C and hardware-model-backed static-recompilation tracks. Outside requested source platforms; do not misclassify its native runtime as host-only source port.
BlitzMax Tempest source exists, but README Atari ST/1990s provenance conflicts with 2005 source header and general arcade lineage; defer platform/provenance qualification.
Substantive AMOS promotional-demo remake, but current request focuses games/applications; retain as adjacent demo lead.
README remains Laravel boilerplate and inspected tree does not establish sufficiently qualified CPC reconstruction; defer.
Fork of Richard-Lloyd/Amstrad-CPC-ROM-Disassembly; listing credits Richard Lloyd. Do not add duplicate fork as independent recovery.
